title: Let’s Play: Understanding the Role of Play in Life and Art

sections.note: In this course students will explore the variety of ways that play is integrated into our socio-cultural fabric. Topics will include key ideas from the history of play, play and nature, play in human development, play in learning, play spaces, games and play, play in art, and the role of play in futurist thinking. Students will develop a broad understanding of the interconnectedness of play in different contexts and move beyond common misconceptions of play as something that is only for children.
sections.title: The Role of Play in Life & Art

title: Special Topics in Game Studies & Design

sections.note: An introduction into the design behind 2D digital games. Students will study the design decisions behind 2D games, what stories that can tell, and the beginning skills to make their own. By the end of the course students will have a design doc and the beginnings of a prototype of their own game.
sections.title: 2D Game Design Web/Mobile

sections.note: This course is designed to build a strong foundation for Game Art Animation. You will become familiar with Blender’s interface and navigating both 2D and 3D workspaces, build a strong working knowledge of the basics for animation and design.
sections.title: Animation for Games

meetings.location: ARR Sch of Info Sciences Bldg

sections.note: Get ready to dive into the exciting world of board game design! Through this dynamic course, you’ll learn about the essential components of board games and how they work together through playing and teaching published games. Then, you'll create your own game inspired by what you’ve learned. With hands-on activities that teach essential design thinking principles incorporated into the comprehensive board game design process, you'll unleash your creativity and refine your game design skills! This class is a perfect elective for building your communication and teamwork skills as well as developing the framework to understand complex concepts like abstraction, modularity, feedback, iteration, visual communication and user experience – All while learning about the booming world of board games. Let’s play! Additional Lab Time is Available on Fridays 4pm - 5:20pm.
sections.title: Intro to Board Game Design

sections.note: This course is designed to build a strong foundation for Game Art Development. You will become familiar with Blender’s interface and navigating the 3-D workspace, build a strong working knowledge of the basics for 3-D modeling and design. You will learn the basic skills needed to create 3d models and apply textures and lighting and get a feel for animating, and rendering. Blender is available for Windows and Mac OS.
sections.title: Intro to 3D Game Art

sections.note: Whether you've seen it in your favorite Tabletop Role Playing game, on a television show like Whose Line is it Anyway, or in person at Second City, improvisation is everywhere. In this course, students will learn and practice basic improvisational techniques, with the goal of exploring fictional characters and scenarios in and around games and game design. Students will also get the opportunity to create new Improv games, and approach the space from a designer's perspective. No theater or game design experience is required!
sections.title: Improv for Games

sections.note: Guided exploration of AI tools and how they can be used to design and build games.
sections.title: AI Systems in Games

sections.note: This course teaches students how to collaboratively generate video game concept art, gain industry perspective, and prepare for the role through a simulated studio’s pre-production lifecycle. Students will leave the class with a visual record of their work to showcase to potential employers. To fully benefit from the course, a level of proficiency and confidence in drawing is recommended. Students can work in either traditional or digital mediums (BYOL for digital).
sections.title: Concept Art for Video Games

sections.note: Long before Hollywood embraced cinematic universes, Japan was pioneering cross-media storytelling through its “media mix” strategy—seamlessly blending manga, anime, games, and novels into expansive narrative worlds. This course dives into the history, creativity, and global impact of Japan’s media mix, inviting students to explore iconic examples and craft their own interconnected media experiences.
sections.title: Japan's "Media Mix"
